## Parent

#1090

## What to build

Verify checked log-sequence-number parsing, formatting, and numeric ordering with Verus, then make named production callers use that same implementation. Pin only the required verification setup and enforce the proof in CI. Review the specification independently, validate inputs at caller boundaries, preserve persisted formats, and exercise malformed inputs, limits, and round trips. Qualify the integrated code against the candidate package.

Named production callers on current `main`: `version::Frontier::merge_from` and its LSN helpers; `scheduler::watermark` and `scheduler::scheduler_loop` safe-bound conversion; `cdc` frontier holdback comparisons; `api::recovery` frontier validation; and `wal_decoder` transition comparison and its separate `lsn_position` parser. Recheck the list before migration. Each listed caller must reach the verified implementation or a checked adapter to it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Intended proof obligations and ordinary Rust builds pass; listed production callers execute the verified implementation.
- [ ] An intentional semantic defect and a verification bypass or skip are rejected for the intended reasons.
- [ ] Database and compatibility tests exercise the integrated code. Existing performance regression checks remain active.
- [ ] Assumptions and unproved boundaries are documented beside the implementation. Public wording claims only the checked LSN operations.
- [ ] #1093 ties verified source and runtime checks to the candidate package before an integrated release claim.

## Blocked by

None (mathematical and build work can start immediately; final qualification uses #1091 and #1093).

## Historical context

Replaces only the LSN foundation and caller scope from #1057–#1061, with applicable adapter and release checks from #1087–#1089. Further proof domains need a separate decision.

# Acceptance contract: #1097

Contract revision: v1
Source: [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), What to build and acceptance criteria; [#1090](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1090), working agreement and completion
Parent contract: [#1090](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1090) v1
Parent snapshot: #1090 acceptance-contract:1090:v1 block in the canonical issue body; SHA-256: c5645654a11745aee1b64549f457348a145cc9dd10d009b351c2ea89c256d982
Contribution: Refines #1090 v1:Q1090-R03, Q1090-R05, and Q1090-R06 for one formally checked production LSN implementation, named caller integration, and candidate binding.
Prerequisites: None to start. An integrated release claim requires #1091 exact-result checks and #1093 candidate qualification; the accepted grammar and pinned verifier are fixed contract inputs.

Intended outcome: Verify checked log-sequence-number parsing, formatting, and numeric ordering with Verus, then make named production callers use that same implementation. Pin only the required verification setup and enforce the proof in CI. Review the specification independently, validate inputs at caller boundaries, preserve persisted formats, and exercise malformed inputs, limits, and round trips. Qualify the integrated code against the candidate package.

## Evidence context

Anchors: [version helpers](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/version.rs),
[watermark](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/scheduler/watermark.rs),
[scheduler loop](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/scheduler/scheduler_loop.rs),
[CDC holdback](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/cdc/mod.rs), [recovery](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/api/recovery.rs), and
[WAL transitions](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/blob/main/src/wal_decoder.rs). Implementation decision: Use PostgreSQL 18's documented pg_lsn grammar: two hexadecimal components, each one to eight digits, separated by '/', with no whitespace or sign, and values in the inclusive range 0/0 through FFFFFFFF/FFFFFFFF. Canonical formatter output remains an uppercase high half and an eight-digit uppercase low half. Pin the official Verus release image ghcr.io/verus-lang/verus:0.2025.06.23.2e59154@sha256:c4d0471379b23c3c6f52e3d7226c7dad28f488c4288e14c623002bd279a745e0 and run its verifier against the checked LSN source with: docker run --rm --pull=never -v "$PWD:/workspace" -w /workspace ghcr.io/verus-lang/verus:0.2025.06.23.2e59154@sha256:c4d0471379b23c3c6f52e3d7226c7dad28f488c4288e14c623002bd279a745e0 verus --verify --triggers-mode silent verification/lsn.rs.

## Acceptance matrix

| ID | Source | Requirement | Boundaries / counterexamples | Seam | Oracle | Planned evidence | Plan state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1097-R01 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), W/AC1 | Accepted LSN parsing returns the mathematical unsigned position without overflow or truncation. | Empty/missing/extra separator, invalid digits, or a half above `FFFFFFFF`; malformed input silently maps to zero. | Checked production LSN parser | Mathematical high×2^32+low and PostgreSQL-compatible grammar | Verus obligation `lsn_parse_value_and_bounds` on the executable parser: accepted halves are in `[0,2^32-1]` and result is `high*2^32+low`. Rust case `test_lsn_checked_parse_rejects_malformed_and_overflow` exercises rejection examples. Use the resolved grammar above; the first task is to implement the checked parser and run the pinned command. | planned |
| Q1097-R02 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), W/AC1 | Formatting round-trips every `u64` through the verified parser. | Zero, low-half rollover, and `u64::MAX`; incorrect shift or missing digit. | Checked production LSN formatter/parser | u64 round-trip identity and known boundary strings | Verus obligation `lsn_format_parse_roundtrip` proves `parse(format(n)) = n` for all `u64` values. Concrete expected strings include `0/00000000`, `1/00000000`, and `FFFFFFFF/FFFFFFFF`. Run this obligation with the pinned command against the executable parser. | planned |
| Q1097-R03 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), W/AC1 | Ordering uses numeric value for every accepted spelling. | `0/A` equals `0/0000000A`; `F/FFFFFFFF` is below `10/0`; string equality gives wrong `>=`. | Checked production LSN comparator and PostgreSQL pg_lsn | Numeric u64 ordering and PostgreSQL pg_lsn | Verus obligation `lsn_numeric_order` proves primitive comparisons agree with parsed numeric order. `test_lsn_order_uses_numeric_value_for_all_spellings` checks these explicit examples against PostgreSQL `pg_lsn`. Frontier collection/merge behavior is checked by runtime callers, not added to the formal proof scope. Run the obligation with the pinned command; caller integration remains in R05 and R07. | planned |
| Q1097-R04 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), W/AC3 | Existing persisted frontier formats remain compatible. | Upgrade cannot read existing JSON LSN strings, or formatting changes low-half padding. | Persisted frontier upgrade and refresh/recovery SQL | Supported predecessor's persisted frontier format | `test_lsn_persisted_frontier_compatibility` in proposed `tests/e2e_lsn_contract_tests.rs`. Load frontiers written by the supported predecessor, exercise refresh/merge/recovery, and require unchanged interpreted positions and supported serialized format. Use real committed LSNs for database workflows; round-trip zero/maximum/rollover serialization fixtures separately. Retain existing upgrade gates. | planned |
| Q1097-R05 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), W/AC1 | Every named caller reaches the same verified implementation or a checked adapter. | A second permissive parser or string comparison remains in one caller. | Named production LSN callers | Single verified executable source and caller inventory | `lsn_caller_inventory` beside the implementation maps Frontier merge/helpers, both scheduler conversion sites, CDC holdback, recovery validation, WAL transition comparison, and `lsn_position` to the checked module. Recheck all parser/comparison call sites before migration. The first implementation task must identify the shared executable source and ordinary Rust build path. | planned |
| Q1097-R06 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), W/AC3 | Invalid boundary input cannot silently reset or advance committed progress. | Malformed stored/user frontier becomes zero, overflows, or produces a partial update. | Recovery SQL, scheduler, CDC and WAL transition inputs | Last committed progress and exact valid-input recovery | `test_lsn_invalid_frontier_preserves_committed_progress` in the proposed LSN E2E target. Exercise public recovery input and isolated malformed catalog fixtures through real scheduler, CDC, and transition workflows. Require contextual rejection or safe refusal, unchanged committed progress/buffers, and exact recovery after valid input. Record which caller was reached. | planned |
| Q1097-R07 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), AC1/AC3 | The integrated implementation builds normally and executes through database callers. | Verus proves a separate model that the extension never calls. | Ordinary Rust build and database workflows | PostgreSQL pg_lsn positions and independently known public rows | `test_lsn_integrated_callers_use_checked_semantics` in the LSN E2E target runs merge, watermark, holdback, recovery, and transition fixtures with spelling/rollover boundaries. Require PostgreSQL-numeric expected positions and exact public results. Pair with ordinary `just fmt`, `just lint`, `just test-unit`, and candidate E2E build/results. | planned |
| Q1097-R08 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), AC2 | An intentional semantic defect is rejected by proof. | Change shift/order arithmetic while keeping the code compilable. | Executable checked LSN source and Verus job | Named proof obligations on altered executable expression | `lsn_proof_semantic_control` changes one executable arithmetic/comparison expression and runs the pinned proof command. Require failure of its named obligation, with the correct baseline passing. Run the baseline and altered-source control with the pinned command. | planned |
| Q1097-R09 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), W/AC2 | Required proof execution cannot be bypassed or skipped in CI. | Remove a required obligation, replace verification with exit 0, or skip the job. | CI proof job and obligation inventory | Required obligation inventory and actual verifier output | `lsn_proof_enforcement_controls`. CI checks the required obligation inventory and actual verifier result, rejects absent obligations/results, and requires the proof job before affected acceptance. Pin the compiler and solver identities alongside the already pinned Verus image and run the enforcement control. | planned |
| Q1097-R10 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), W/AC4 | The specification receives independent review and states assumptions/unproved boundaries beside the code. | Proof assumes its conclusion, grammar differs from callers, or public wording claims whole-extension correctness. | Specification review artifact beside executable source | Independent reviewer and explicit trusted assumptions | `lsn_specification_review` records an independent reviewer, specification/source revision, accepted grammar, mathematical definitions, trusted adapters, toolchain assumptions, and excluded behavior. Review occurs before claiming the obligations establish the intended contract. | planned |
| Q1097-R11 | [#1097](https://github.com/trickle-labs/pg-trickle/issues/1097), AC5 | An integrated release claim binds verified executable source to the tested candidate. | Proof from commit A accompanies a package built from different LSN source B. | Release qualification evidence | Verified source digest versus built and installed candidate digest | `check_lsn_proof_candidate_binding` extends #1093. Require pinned proof result and executable-source digest, candidate build provenance, installed candidate digests, and LSN runtime case identities. A source-mismatch control must fail. Existing performance gates remain required under Q1093-R14. | planned |

## Unresolved gaps

- None. The grammar and verifier/toolchain are now fixed contract inputs; implementation still must create and run them.

## Open questions

- None.

## Out of scope

- Proof families beyond checked LSN operations and whole-extension verification claims.

## Change notes

- The v1 planning inputs are now explicit: PostgreSQL 18 grammar and a pinned official Verus image/command. Requirement meanings are unchanged.- Initial contract, v1. Existing matrix IDs Q1097-R01–Q1097-R11 retain their meanings; GitHub issue history preserves the prior matrix. The original acceptance checkboxes remain source criteria, not proof.

## Storage handoff

Canonical destination: this issue body, revision v1. Reread this saved issue before use.

## Implementation handoff

Implement the smallest complete solution inside the spec envelope. Preserve requirement IDs and promised outcomes.

## Proof handoff

Evaluate every requirement against this contract revision and one fixed candidate. Record actual evidence and verdicts in a separate proof report.
